english: Let $L_1$ be the line of intersection of the planes $x+y=3$ and $y-z=1$, and let $L_2$ be the line passing through the points $(3,4,-3)$ and $(5,4,1)$. The line of shortest distance between $L_1$ and $L_2$ meets $L_1$ at the point $P$ and $L_2$ at the point $Q$. If $O$ is the origin, then the value of $OP^{2}+OQ^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $L_1$ तलों $x+y=3$ तथा $y-z=1$ की प्रतिच्छेदन रेखा है, तथा $L_2$ बिन्दुओं $(3,4,-3)$ और $(5,4,1)$ से होकर जाने वाली रेखा है। $L_1$ तथा $L_2$ के बीच की न्यूनतम दूरी की रेखा $L_1$ से बिन्दु $P$ पर तथा $L_2$ से बिन्दु $Q$ पर मिलती है। यदि $O$ मूलबिन्दु है, तो $OP^{2}+OQ^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: $L_1$ lies in both planes, so its direction is perpendicular to both normals: $(1,1,0)\times(0,1,-1)=(1\cdot(-1)-0\cdot1,\ 0\cdot0-1\cdot(-1),\ 1\cdot1-1\cdot0)=(-1,1,1)$.
Putting $y=0$ in the two equations gives $x=3$, $z=-1$, so $(3,0,-1)\in L_1$ and a general point is $P(3-t,\,t,\,t-1)$.
$L_2$ has direction $(5-3,4-4,1+3)=(2,0,4)$, that is $(1,0,2)$, and a general point is $Q(3+s,\,4,\,-3+2s)$.
So $P=(2,1,0)$ and $Q=(4,4,-1)$; $\overrightarrow{PQ}=(2,3,-1)$, and $(-1,1,1)\times(1,0,2)=(2,3,-1)$, as expected. The line of shortest distance is $\dfrac{x-2}{2}=\dfrac{y-1}{3}=\dfrac{z}{-1}$.
originality_note: New: one line is given only as the intersection of two planes and the other only through two points, so the directions must be built (cross product of normals, difference of points) before the common perpendicular is found (way 5). Closest known: feet of the common perpendicular of two lines in symmetric form. Different because: neither line is given in symmetric form and the answer depends on both feet, not on the distance.
blueprint_concepts: Shortest Distance Line Equation: Finding the symmetrical equation of the line of shortest distance between skew lines.

concept_use.Shortest Distance Line Equation: Finding: PQ perpendicular to both directions (-1,1,1) and (1,0,2) gives t = s = 1, the feet P(2,1,0), Q(4,4,-1) and the line (x-2)/2 = (y-1)/3 = z/(-1).
